title: ScenarioSourceV2
description:
A version-2 scenario document.

Version 2 replaces the version-1 `profiles`/`pedestrian_profiles`,
`population`, `demand`, and `pedestrian_demand` fields with `mode_templates`
and a mode-tagged `demand`, and makes each movement's `direction` explicit.
The Increment 1 additive arrays `facilities`, `facility_connectors`, and
`permissions` extend it in place, and Increment 2 adds
`facility_adjacencies`, `clearance_bands`, and `maneuver_policy` the same
way. Every other version-1 field is carried forward unchanged.

boundaries.description: Closed polygons marking the non-traversable world limits.

clearance_bands.description:
Scenario-scoped clearance-band definitions, declared in strictly
increasing thresholds. Additive Increment 2 array; omitted or empty
means close-pass observations carry no band durations or violations.

conflict_regions.description: Authored conflict regions shared by pairs of movements.

coordinate_system.description: Human-facing names for the two world axes.

crossings.description: Pedestrian crossings over one or more movements.

demand.description: Mode-tagged demand sources for every mode.

facilities.description:
Continuous-width facilities with usable width, nominal direction, mode
access, lateral-use policy, and speed policy. Additive Increment 1
array; omitted or empty means no facilities.

facility_adjacencies.description:
Side-by-side facility pairs that permit a lateral transition between
them. Additive Increment 2 array; omitted or empty means no lateral
transitions exist.

facility_connectors.description:
Directed connectors joining two facility traversals. Additive
Increment 1 array.

id.description: Stable scenario identifier recorded in run provenance.

maneuver_policy.description:
Scenario-scoped commit and wrong-way policy. Additive Increment 2
object; omitted means no lateral tactic or wrong-way decision is
authored.

mode_templates.description: Named, validated mode bundles; demand references them by id.

movements.description: Movement connectors with an explicit nominal direction.

pedestrian_routes.description: Pedestrian routes from one portal to another along a guide path.

permissions.description:
Authored permission and obligation statements. Additive Increment 1
array; the shape is fixed in full, while only `nominal_direction`
statements are populated in Increment 1.

portals.description: Entry and exit points attached to path ends.

regions.description: Closed polygons marking traversable areas other than guide paths.

rules.description: Right-of-way or control rules attached to movements.

schema_version.description: Schema version the document was written against.

signals.description: Fixed-time signal controllers with phased signal heads.

waiting_areas.description: Named waiting areas where pedestrians stage before crossing.

AccessSource.description: Facility access of a version-2 mode template.

facility_kinds.description: Traversable object kinds the mode may use.

nominal_direction.description:
Direction the mode may travel on its facilities.

Omitted means `either`, the value Increment 0 fixed for the compiled
access direction because nothing authored it. Additive Increment 1
field: an Increment 0 template omits it and keeps that meaning.

speed_policy.description:
Speed policy the mode travels under.

Omitted means no enforced limit, the value Increment 0 fixed for the
compiled access. Additive Increment 1 field.

AdjacencySide.description:
Side of the `first` facility on which the `second` lies, measured in
`first`'s authored forward direction.

oneOf.description: The positive-`d` side of `first`'s authored forward direction.
The negative-`d` side of `first`'s authored forward direction.

ClearanceBandSource.description:
One scenario-scoped clearance band: a labeled body-to-body signed surface
clearance threshold.

Bands are metric definitions for the scenario that authors them, never
universal declarations of safety. A band accumulates the duration during
which the observed clearance is below its `threshold_m`, so bands declared
in strictly increasing threshold nest.

applies_to_modes.description:
Mode-template ids the band applies to. An absent field means the band
applies to every mode pair; a present list must be non-empty, so an
authored empty list is distinguishable from an omitted one.

id.description: Stable id, unique across all authored objects.

threshold_m.description: Signed surface clearance threshold the band defines, in metres.

violation.description:
Whether a pass below `threshold_m` is recorded as a lateral-displacement
violation in this scenario.

CommitPolicySource.description:
The unsafe-commit and commitment-loss policy of a version-2 scenario.

Every field is required once `commit` is present; nothing defaults.

hold_timeout_s.description:
How long a `preparing` maneuver may wait for a granted claim, and how
long a `committed` maneuver may hold at or below its target clearance
waiting for the corridor to reopen, before it aborts. Seconds.

min_predicted_clearance_m.description:
Absolute floor on the predicted minimum clearance of any of the four
clearance facts, in metres; a committed maneuver whose predicted
clearance falls below it aborts.

ConflictRegionSource.description:
An authored conflict region shared by two movements.

The geometry lets a renderer or metric show where two movement envelopes
cross; the movement pair is what a signal check uses to reject conflicting
greens. A scenario may author it explicitly or, later, accept a derived one.

id.description: Stable identifier, unique across all authored objects.

movements.description: Exactly two movements whose envelopes conflict in this region.

CoordinateSystem.description: Human-facing names for the world coordinate axes.

x.description: Name of the positive x axis, for example `east_m`.

y.description: Name of the positive y axis, for example `north_m`.

CrossingSource.description: A pedestrian crossing occupying a traversable region over some movements.

id.description: Stable identifier, unique across all authored objects.

pedestrian_signal.description:
Fixed-time pedestrian signal rule for this crossing.

Omitted (the default) is an uncontrolled crossing: pedestrians cross it
freely, subject to ordinary interaction. Additive schema version 1
field, mirroring the `stop_line_m`/`compliance` precedent.

DemandChoiceSource.description:
Choice of movements or routes for a version-2 rate demand spawn.

Vehicle modes choose among movements; pedestrian modes choose among
pedestrian routes.

oneOf.description: Movements a generated vehicle may follow, with relative weights.
Pedestrian routes a generated pedestrian may follow, with weights.

DemandPopulationSpawnSource.description: A fixed initial-population version-2 demand spawn, placed at `t = 0`.

count.description: Number of agents in the population.

path.description: Guide path the population is placed on.

spacing_m.description: Longitudinal gap between adjacent agents in metres.

speed_mps.description: Constant speed in metres per second.

choice.description: Movements or routes a generated agent may follow.

interval_s.description: Interval over which the rate applies.

portal.description: Entry portal where generated agents enter the world.

rate_per_hour.description: Mean arrival rate in agents per hour.

id.description: Stable identifier, unique across all authored objects.

DemandSpawnSource.description: How a version-2 demand source places agents.

oneOf.description: Arrivals at a portal over a time interval.
A fixed population placed at `t = 0`.

FacilityAccessSource.description: Mode-template access of a version-2 facility.

modes.description: Mode-template ids permitted to use the facility; non-empty.

FacilityAdjacencySource.description:
Two version-2 facility bands lying side by side along a shared stretch.

This is the only lateral-transition relation: a [`FacilityConnectorSource`]
keeps its Increment 1 meaning of an end join, and proximity alone never
infers a transition.

id.description: Stable id, unique across all authored objects.

second.description: Id of a declared facility adjacent to `first`.

side.description:
Side of `first` on which `second` lies, in `first`'s authored forward
direction (its reference path vertex order).

FacilityConnectorEndSource.description: One end of a version-2 facility connector.

direction.description: Traversal direction along that facility: `forward` or `reverse`.

FacilityConnectorSource.description: A version-2 directed connector joining two facility traversals.

from.description: Facility and traversal direction the connector leaves.

id.description: Stable connector id, unique across all authored objects.

to.description: Facility and traversal direction the connector enters.

FacilityDirection.description:
Direction a mode may travel along a facility reference path, relative to
the authored vertex order of that path.

oneOf.description: Only the authored forward direction.
Only the reverse of the authored direction.
Either direction.

FacilityKind.description: Traversable object kind a version-2 mode may use.

oneOf.description: A guide path.
A pedestrian crossing.
A pedestrian waiting area.

A continuous-width facility: a region with an optional reference path.
Additive Increment 1 kind, so an Increment 0 template keeps its meaning.

FacilityLateralPolicySource.description:
A version-2 facility's lateral-use policy. Additive Increment 2 object:
omitted means the facility offers no lateral maneuver target and behaves
exactly as in Increment 1.

passing_side.description: Side on which a pass or overtake on this facility displaces.

FacilitySource.description:
One version-2 continuous-width facility: a traversable region plus an
optional reference path, usable width, nominal direction, mode access,
lateral-use policy, speed policy, and optional lateral-maneuver policy.

access.description: Mode templates permitted to use the facility.

id.description: Stable facility id, unique across all authored objects.

lateral_policy.description:
Side a pass or overtake on this facility displaces toward. Additive
Increment 2 object; omitted means the facility offers no lateral
maneuver target, the Increment 1 behaviour.

lateral_use.description: Whether the usable lateral interval is shared or centered.

nominal_direction.description:
Nominal direction relative to the authored vertex order of
`reference_path`.

reference_path.description:
Guide path giving the facility its `(s, d)` frame; omitted means the
facility exposes region geometry only.

speed_policy.description: Speed policy on the facility; a missing field is a parse error.

width_m.description: Usable traversable width in metres, measured across the reference path.

LateralUse.description:
Whether a facility's usable lateral interval is one shared space or a
centered lane.

oneOf.description: Agents may occupy any position within the usable lateral interval.
Agents hold the reference centerline.

ManeuverPolicySource.description:
Scenario-scoped maneuver policy. Additive Increment 2 object: omitted means
no lateral tactic or wrong-way decision is authored, and the document
behaves exactly as in Increment 1.

`commit` and `wrong_way` are optional inside it, so a scenario that authors
only lateral tactics omits `wrong_way`, and one that authors no lateral
policy at all omits the whole object.

ModeBodySource.description: Body geometry distributions of one version-2 mode template.

oneOf.description: A rectangular body; dimensions are ranges in metres.
A circular body; the radius is a range in metres.

A capsule body: a segment of `length_m` with a constant `radius_m`.

Additive Increment 1 kind for the narrow wheeled family; it compiles to
the existing `AgentBody::Capsule` and the `wheeled_capsule` family.

ModeLateralSource.description:
The lateral maneuver parameters of one version-2 mode template. Additive
Increment 2 object: omitted means the mode has no free lateral motion, no
lateral maneuver is selectable, and the mode behaves exactly as in
Increment 1.

horizon_s.description:
Feasible time horizon in seconds: a candidate corridor is feasible only
while it stays feasible at least this long from the decision instant.

target_clearance_m.description:
Signed body-to-body surface clearance, in metres, the mode targets
between its own swept envelope and the envelope of the body it is
passing or overtaking, at the maneuver's closest approach.

ModeTemplateSource.description:
One version-2 mode template: a named, validated bundle of body, motion,
tactical capability, access, occupancy, and profile distributions.

access.description: Traversable object kinds the mode may use.

id.description: Stable template id, unique across authored objects.

lateral.description:
The mode's own lateral maneuver parameters. Additive Increment 2 field:
omitted means the mode has no free lateral motion and behaves exactly as
in Increment 1.

profiles.description: Profile distributions keyed by parameter name.

MotionKind.description: Motion family a version-2 mode template uses.

oneOf.description: Walking on the Phase 1 pedestrian geometry.
A single wheeled body following a reference path.

MovementDirection.description: Nominal traversal direction of a version-2 movement along its reference path.

oneOf.description: The movement follows the authored vertex order of its path.
The movement follows the reverse of the authored vertex order.

MovementSourceV2.description:
A version-2 movement connector with an explicit nominal direction.

Every version-1 movement field is carried forward unchanged; version 2 adds
`direction` so the normalized document is self-describing instead of leaving
the direction implicit in the `from`/`to` portal order.

id.description: Stable identifier, unique across all authored objects.

priority.description: Right-of-way rank; a lower value is honored before a higher one.

stop_line_m.description: Stop-line arc length in metres from the movement entry.

OccupancyKind.description: Occupancy of a version-2 mode template.

oneOf.description: One operator, no passengers.

PassingSide.description:
Side on which a within-facility pass or overtake displaces, measured in the
maneuvering agent's own direction of travel on the facility.

oneOf.description: The positive-`d` side.
The negative-`d` side.

The side whose usable corridor has the greater predicted minimum
clearance; an exact tie resolves to `left`.

PathEnd.description: Which end of a path a portal is attached to.

oneOf.description: The first vertex of the path.
The last vertex of the path.

PathSource.description: One authored guide path as an ordered polyline.

id.description: Stable path identifier, unique across all authored objects.

points.description: Ordered vertices of the guide path.

PedestrianRouteShareSource.description:
One pedestrian route's relative share of a pedestrian demand source's
arrivals.

route.description: Pedestrian route a generated pedestrian follows.

weight.description: Relative weight; a larger weight is chosen proportionally more often.

PedestrianRouteSource.description:
A pedestrian route from one portal to another along a guide path.

A route is the pedestrian routing primitive, mirroring [`MovementSource`]
for the vehicle mode. It reuses the same path geometry and portals, and
additionally names the crossings and waiting areas it passes through in
travel order, so signal compliance and staging can be attached per route
without naming a scenario kind.

crossings.description: Crossings the route traverses, in travel order.

id.description: Stable identifier, unique across all authored objects.

waiting_areas.description: Waiting areas the route stages at, in travel order.

walk.description: Whether pedestrians may cross during this phase.

PedestrianSignalSource.description:
A fixed-time pedestrian signal rule embedded in one crossing.

It is the pedestrian analogue of [`SignalSource`] but its controlled object
is the owning crossing rather than a movement, so a pedestrian rule needs no
vehicle signal. Its phases alternate a walk interval, during which crossing
is permitted, and a don't-walk interval, during which the signal forbids
crossing; the phases are contiguous and cover the cycle.

PermissionEffect.description: Whether a permission statement permits, prohibits, or obligates.

oneOf.description: The holder may do the statement's action.
The holder must not do it.
The holder must do it.

PermissionKind.description: What an authored permission or obligation statement is about.

oneOf.description: Travel against a facility's or movement's nominal direction.
Permitted lateral position or lane use on a facility.
Overtaking or passing on a facility.
Permission or obligation at a crossing.
Stop-service obligation and priority.

PermissionSource.description: One authored permission or obligation statement.

effect.description: Whether the statement permits, prohibits, or obligates.

id.description: Stable id, unique across all authored objects.

kind.description: Kind of statement; it fixes the target object kind.

target.description: Id of the object the statement is about.

PolygonSource.description:
A closed polygon in metres.

The ring closes implicitly from the last vertex back to the first, so the
authored vertex list must not repeat the first point at the end.

id.description: Stable identifier, unique across all authored objects.

PortalSource.description: An entry or exit point attached to one end of a path.

end.description: Which end of the path the portal marks.

id.description: Stable portal identifier, unique across all authored objects.

path.description: Identifier of the path this portal belongs to.

width_m.description: Traversable width of the portal in metres.

ProfileRangeSource.description:
An inclusive uniform distribution for one profile parameter.

A range with `min == max` is a constant. The owning field name carries the
physical unit, for example `speed_mps` or `time_gap_s`.

RouteShareSource.description: One movement's relative share of a demand source's arrivals.

weight.description: Relative weight; a larger weight is chosen proportionally more often.

RuleKind.description: How a movement's right of way is controlled.

oneOf.description: No control; the movement proceeds subject to ordinary interaction.
The movement must yield to the conflicting movements.
The movement must stop before proceeding.
A signal controller governs the movement.

RuleSource.description: A control rule attached to one movement.

id.description: Stable identifier, unique across all authored objects.

kind.description: Kind of control the rule applies.

signal.description: Signal controller, present exactly when `kind` is `signal`.

SignalColor.description: Display color of one signal head during one phase.

oneOf.description: The controlled movement must stop.
The controlled movement should prepare to stop.
The controlled movement may proceed.

SignalHeadSource.description: One signal head controlling a movement.

id.description: Identifier unique within the owning signal.

states.description: The color of every head in the owning signal during this phase.

id.description: Stable identifier, unique across all authored objects.

phases.description: Phases in cycle order, each showing every head once.

SignalStateSource.description: One head's color during one phase.

color.description: Color shown on that head during this phase.

head.description: Head identifier within the owning signal.

SpeedLimitMps.description:
An enforced speed limit: a finite positive value, or an explicit `null` for
no enforced limit beyond the mode's own motion limits.

The value is a required, nullable field, so an absent `limit_mps` is a parse
error rather than a silent default; a present `null` is the explicit "no
limit" form and mirrors the unbounded `TimeIntervalSource.end_s` precedent.
Deserialization is written by hand so a missing field is rejected: serde's
`Option`-derived newtype would otherwise treat absence as `null`.

SpeedPolicySource.description: A speed policy: a finite positive limit, or none.

limit_mps.description: Enforced limit in metres per second; `null` means no enforced limit.

TacticKind.description:
Tactical capability a version-2 mode template supports.

The Increment 0 values `follow`, `stop`, and `yield` keep their meaning and
their compiled mapping. Additive Increment 2 values `change_lane`,
`overtake`, `pass`, and `reverse_direction` extend the same field in place,
so a template that declares none of them compiles exactly as before.

oneOf.description: Follow the agent ahead.
Stop for a control or an obstruction.
Yield to a conflicting movement.
Move laterally to an adjacent facility traversal.
Displace past a slower leader on the facility.
Pass a slower user within the same facility.
Select a traversal against the applicable nominal direction.

TimeIntervalSource.description: The time interval of a version-2 rate demand spawn.

end_s.description: Interval end in seconds; `null` is unbounded.

WaitingAreaSource.description:
A named waiting area where pedestrians stage between crossings.

The area is the region itself; the named reference gives a pedestrian route
a stable object to wait at and a later increment a place to attach staging
behavior. It traverses no movement and carries no control of its own.

id.description: Stable identifier, unique across all authored objects.

region.description: Traversable region the waiting area occupies.

WrongWayPolicySource.description:
The contextual opposing-traversal decision inputs of a version-2 scenario.

Every field is required once `wrong_way` is present; nothing defaults.

max_opposing_density_per_km.description:
Largest density of opposing-travelling bodies, in agents per kilometre,
observed within the target traversal ahead for which the opposing option
stays eligible.

min_time_saving_s.description:
Minimum estimated travel-time saving, in seconds, the opposing option
must provide over the nominal option.

urgency.description:
The scenario's willingness in `[0, 1]` to accept a violating opposing
traversal.
